issue_context.summary: New+ hiding the built-in New context menu breaks File Explorer Ctrl+Shift+N.
known_information: The issue is open and labeled Issue-Bug, Product-File Explorer, Product-New+, and Needs-Triage.
The reporter provides a direct reproduction: enabling Hide the built-in "New" context menu immediately breaks Ctrl+Shift+N, and disabling it restores the shortcut without restarting Explorer.
The report includes registry evidence showing HKCU\\Software\\Classes\\Directory\\Background\\shellex\\ContextMenuHandlers\\New set to disabled_ while HKLM still points at the native handler.
A comment confirms the problem on stable v0.101.2362.0.
The issue was last updated on 2026-09-12T16:24:09Z.
inferences: PowerToys is mutating the per-user handler in a way that shadows the native Explorer implementation used by both the menu and Ctrl+Shift+N.
The failure is deterministic and tied to the hide setting itself, not to Explorer restart timing.
issue_context.analysis: The public evidence already isolates the registry mutation and makes a migration-focused fix design appropriate.
initial_investigation: Read the live issue body, labels, and comment thread.
Compared the reported registry state with the current New+ behavior described in the issue.

verify: Build the affected New+ and Settings targets.
Verify Explorer and common-dialog folder creation.
alternatives: Emulating native folder creation was rejected as fragile and unsupported.
